valuation_insights:
Apple Inc. reported a fiscal 2026 total revenue of $478.83 billion, growing approximately 15.1% year over year [C:revenue_growth]. This strong top-line growth was accompanied by an operating income of $158.06 billion, yielding an operating margin of 33.0% based on total revenue [C:operating_margin]. For context, Microsoft’s fiscal 2026 operating margin was 46.8%, Alphabet's 32.0%, and Oracle's 30.6% on a comparable total-revenue basis, as sourced from their respective 10-K filings (Microsoft accession 0000789019-26-000054, Alphabet accession 0001652044-26-000021, Oracle accession 0001341439-26-000033). Net income attributable to the company reached $132.18 billion with a notable return on average equity of 142.3% [C:return_on_average_equity], reflecting highly effective use of shareholder equity capital. Apple’s diluted EPS was $8.98, delivering a price-to-earnings ratio of about 38.4 based on the closing price of $344.63 on October 30, 2026 [C:pe], suggesting a market premium valuation relative to earnings. The company’s total debt (including current portion) to equity ratio stands at 0.70 [C:debt_to_equity], reflecting moderate leverage. Free cash flow was robust at $136.06 billion, calculated as net cash provided by operating activities minus capital expenditures, both sourced from the fiscal 2026 10-K [C:free_cash_flow], supporting continued shareholder returns and investment. Quarterly revenue for Q4 2026 was $114.48 billion, up 12% year over year per earnings release [C:quarter_revenue, C:quarter_revenue_growth], and the diluted EPS was $2.10 [C:quarter_diluted_eps]. 

Insight: Beyond headline growth, Apple’s substantial operating income expansion accompanied by tariff-related margin benefits indicates strategic cost management and pricing power, detailed in the earnings release at lines 12 and 40 [L000012, L000040].

identity: As the Financial Analyst at our desk, I provide an independent, data-driven perspective focusing on rigorously sourced financial metrics from SEC filings and official disclosures. My analysis emphasizes transparency of sources and precise alignment with GAAP standards to ensure credibility and comparability across companies.
reading_approach: I prioritize income-statement line items directly tagged in XBRL such as RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax for total revenue, OperatingIncomeLoss for operating income, and NetIncomeLoss for net income. For cash flow, NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities and PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment are closely reviewed. On the balance sheet, I focus on StockholdersEquity and LongTermDebt tags including current portions, avoiding shortcuts like mixing net sales with total revenue or using unofficial definitions.
data_given: All financial facts, calculator outputs, release excerpt lines, and peer operating margin comparisons from fiscal 2026 filings and exhibits constitute the full evidence set I employ, explicitly excluding any external data or non-supplied assumptions.
scored_criteria: Our team scores fiscal quality via total revenue tagged 'RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax' for FY2026 (2026-09-26), growth from prior year filings, leverage using debt-to-equity ratios from the balance sheet at fiscal year-end, operating margin against total revenue, and valuation metrics such as P/E derived from share price on 2026-10-30 and fiscal EPS. Operating margin comparisons are solidified by referencing peer 10-K filings for Microsoft, Alphabet, and Oracle for the same fiscal period.
what_changes_my_view: A revision in revenue definitions that clarifies treatment of membership or other non-contract revenue components, or a material change in debt classification on the balance sheet, would prompt reassessment. Additionally, quarterly segment disclosures differing from total revenue tags or a notable change in GAAP EPS calculations in the next 10-K would alter my financial outlook.
output_and_insight: I own the Valuation Insights wording and ensure each numeric claim is fully sourced with XBRL tags, line quotes, or calculated ratios with inputs cited. My Insight beyond the headline highlights Apple’s operating income growth aided by tariff-related margin favorable impacts, indicating operational leverage and pricing power beyond top-line expansion as documented in the filing lines 12 (earnings release) and 40 (net sales) of the 10-K.
